evidence: Clicking New Resume created 'Untitled Resume' with empty contact fields, empty summary (0/500 chars), empty experience list; user could type immediately into fields.

Experience/education start/end date inputs are native type=month fields (consistent month/year format). Checking 'I currently work here' on an experience entry cleared its end-date value to '' and disabled the field.

issue: No validation for invalid experience date ranges
actual: Set experience start date to 2020-01 and end date to 2019-01 (end before start). No error message or validation feedback appeared; the invalid value was accepted, persisted across tab switches, and rendered in preview as 'Jan 2020 - Jan 2019' without rejection.

evidence: Entered contact details & summary (reflected live); added/edited/reordered (move up/down) two experience entries; added/edited/reordered/removed education entries; added a skill with level, changed its level (Expert->Advanced), and removed a second skill.

Switched between Modern, Classic, and Minimal templates via editor.template.item.*; each applied a different visual style (casing, separators) while retaining all contact, summary, experience, education, and skills content.

Every field edit (contact, summary, experience, education, skills) and every template switch was reflected in the preview.document observables immediately after the action, with no save or refresh performed.

Moved Education section above Experience (order updated in both editor list and preview), toggled Skills section visibility off (section disappeared from preview) and back on (reappeared), and edited a section heading which updated live.
Section reorder and visibility toggle changes appeared in the preview immediately without save/refresh; will further confirm persistence when navigating within session under CT-16/IX-14.

Clicked Hide Preview (preview region disappeared, editor content still present), then Show Preview again; all contact, summary, education, experience, skills content and the Modern template selection were intact and shown correctly.

issue: No validation feedback shown when renaming to whitespace-only title
actual: Editing the resume title to '   ' (whitespace only) and pressing Enter correctly kept the title as 'Untitled Resume' (did not save the empty title), but no error message, toast, or any visible validation feedback was shown to the user; the field simply silently reverted to display mode.

evidence: Renamed resume from 'Untitled Resume' to 'QA Test Resume'; editor title showed 'QA Test Resume' and dashboard card for resume 'yeymeoi0z7d' also showed 'QA Test Resume'.

After editing fields across multiple editor tabs and renaming the resume, returning to the dashboard showed the resume as 'Updated Aug 25, 2026' (today) at the top of the Newest First sorted list with the new title, confirming edits were retained and reflected on the dashboard.

After returning to dashboard and reopening 'QA Test Resume', all contact details, summary, education, experience entries, skills, custom section heading ('Career History'), section order, and section visibility were fully intact.

Added 10 experience entries to force overflow (document scrollHeight 4682 vs viewport 720); all visible sections with content (summary, education, 10 experience entries, skills) rendered in preview.document, and the page/preview area was scrollable (window.scrollTo reached full content) so the complete resume remained reachable.

issue: Contact section's customizable heading is never rendered in preview
actual: The Sections editor allows customizing the Contact section heading (editor.sections.item.contact.title, changed to 'MY CONTACT DETAILS'). This custom text never appeared in the preview for any of the three styles (Modern, Classic, Minimal), even though the Contact section itself is visible with content. Other section headings (Summary, Education, Experience, Skills) did render their customized text correctly in Modern/Classic, but Minimal also omitted the Summary section heading entirely while still showing the summary text.

evidence: Used card menu > Duplicate on 'QA Test Resume' to create 'QA Test Resume (Copy)' with identical content; renamed the copy to 'QA Test Resume - Marketing Version' and edited its contact name to 'Jane Marketing Doe'; the source resume's title and full name remained 'QA Test Resume' / 'Jane Doe' respectively.

Editing the copy's full name to 'Jane Marketing Doe' did not change the original ('Jane Doe' persisted). Then editing the original's full name to 'Jane Original Doe' did not change the copy (still showed 'Jane Marketing Doe') when reopened.

Dashboard lists 5 distinct resume variations simultaneously ('QA Test Resume - Marketing Version', 'QA Test Resume', 'Product Designer Resume', 'Marketing Manager Resume', 'Software Engineer Resume'), each independently created/edited during the session.

Searching 'marketing' (lowercase) matched both 'Marketing Manager Resume' and 'QA Test Resume - Marketing Version' (case-insensitive); searching 'SOFTWARE' (uppercase) matched 'Software Engineer Resume'; clearing search restored all 5 resumes. Sorting 'Oldest First' ordered resumes chronologically ascending by date, and 'Newest First' reversed the order correctly.

issue: No date filter control exists on the dashboard
actual: The dashboard only offers a title search box (dashboard.search) and a sort dropdown (Newest/Oldest/Title A-Z/Title Z-A). There is no control to filter/narrow resumes by an exact creation date or a date range anywhere on the page (full accessibility snapshot confirms no such input exists).

issue: Resume data is not persisted across page reloads
actual: Created 'QA Test Resume' with full contact/summary/experience/education/skills content, edited it, renamed it, duplicated it (renaming and editing the copy), and deleted the copy. After reloading the application (browser_navigate to the same URL), 'QA Test Resume' had completely disappeared from the dashboard; only the original 3 seed resumes (Product Designer, Marketing Manager, Software Engineer) remained. All created/edited/renamed/duplicated work was lost on reload, and it could not be verified whether the deletion itself would have persisted since the whole resume vanished regardless.
